`python3 -m unittest -q` now passes (7 tests, OK). I made two code fixes in `household/bills.py` and changed one test expectation.

- **`split_bill`**: it dropped the leftover cents, so `split_bill(1001, 2)` gave `[500, 500]`. It now uses `divmod` and gives one extra cent each to the first `total % people` people, as the docstring says.
- **`due_dates`**: the month was `first.month + i` with no year rollover, so a schedule running past December raised `IllegalMonthError` (month 13). It now computes the year and month with `divmod(first.month - 1 + i, 12)`.
- **Test change**: `test_three_ways` expected `split_bill(1000, 3) == [333, 333, 333]`. That sums to 999, which contradicts the docstring's "shares add up to exactly total_cents" and the remainder test. I changed it to `[334, 333, 333]`. That test only passed before because of the bug, so check you agree with that reading.
